newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait oil firm KPC reports rise in 1996 profits.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait oil firm KPC reports rise in 1996 profits.

text.p: State-owned Kuwait Petroleum Corp's (KPC) net profits rose by almost $200 million in 1996 to 870.8 million dinars ($2.88 billion), newspapers said on Friday.

KPC's annual report put total revenues for 1996 at 5.9 billion dinars compare with 5.4 billion in 1995. Total assets at the end of 1996 were 8.28 billion dinars compared with 8.24 billion the previous year, the daily al-Rai al-Aam said.
KPC, one of the world's 10 largest oil firms, is in charge of the country's oil industry and also operates refining and downstream networks abroad.
The report said Kuwait's crude exports rose slightly last year to 1.07 million barrels per day (bpd) from 1.06 million. Refined products exports were little changed at 697,000 bpd in 1996.

Kuwait's domestic refining capacity grew over the past year to reach 895,000 bpd by the end of 1996. The report said KPC planned a global refined product production capacity of 1.6 million bpd by early in the next century, including a 900,000 bpd output at home and 400,000 bpd from new projects in Asia.

Kuwait, which has an OPEC crude quota of two million bpd, is in advanced negotiations with several Asian states to launch new refineries or take a stake and modernise existing ones to penetrate their energy-hungry markets. It controls about 10 percent of the world's proven oil reserves.
The report said KPC's Africa operations boomed last year with exports to South Africa reaching 100,000 bpd from 30,000 bpd.

KPC has several subsidiaries including Kuwait Oil Co, Kuwait National Petroleum Co, Petrochemicals Industries Co, Kuwait Oil Tanker Co, Kuwait Petroleum International, Kuwait Foreign Petroleum Exploration Co and Santa Fe's drilling unit.
KPC, which has a distribution network in Europe, plans to shed about 30 percent of its wholly owned Santa Fe in an initial public offering later this month. ($1=0.302 dinars)
